facts.fact: Tom Allen and Jack Knifton of Manchester were matched for £200 a side and the championship of the world, to fight in England about four weeks later.
Tom Allen and Charley Davis were matched in early 1878 for £100 a side and the English championship, with forfeit money posted.
facts.conflict: amount posted: £40 (604.c1, Feb 24) vs £50 as of Feb 13 (606.c1); match type: a glove match for £100 a side (604.c1) vs a prize fight for £200 at catch weights under the London prize-ring rules (605.c1, low)

facts.fact: In November 1878 Johnny Minan of San Francisco offered to match an unknown fighter, said to be Tom Allen, for $1,000 or $2,000 a side against Paddy Ryan, Mike McCoole or others.
In May 1879 John Dwyer, after beating Jimmy Elliott, said he wanted to fight Tom Allen and offered a £10 forfeit to Bell's Life for a match.
facts.conflict: venue: Dwyer was willing to go to England (626.c2) vs a fight in America if Allen were brought over (629.c1)

facts.fact: In June 1879 Tom Allen of St. Louis agreed, conditionally, to accept John Dwyer's challenge for the championship of America, and said he would cover the $250 Dwyer posted with Frank Queen.
facts.conflict: stake unreadable in the OCR ("$2 gg", probably $2,000) in 630.c1

facts.fact: On November 20, 1879, Tom Allen, then in London, issued a challenge to fight John Dwyer or any man at catch weights for $1,000 a side, in Canada within 100 miles of Buffalo or within 50 miles of Pittsburg.
In May 1880 Alfred Greenfield, the English heavyweight, challenged Tom Allen for £200 or £500, or for a £1,000 champion trophy, and Allen posted a forfeit to meet him in a sixteen-foot ring.
facts.conflict: terms: £200 or £500, or a £1,000 champion trophy (635.c1) vs £200 a side and a champion cup valued at £200 (635.c3, low)

facts.fact: In December 1880 Tom Allen said no would-be champion in England would take £50 or £100 and fight him for it.
